handoff_notes: SqliteAdapter transaction callbacks MUST be synchronous — async callbacks throw TypeError. This is a fundamental better-sqlite3 constraint.
TursoAdapter exec() splits multi-statement SQL on semicolons and executes each statement individually because @libsql/client.execute() only runs the first statement.

SqliteAdapter execute methods use Promise.resolve() wrapping WITHOUT the async keyword — this ensures SQL errors propagate synchronously for transaction rollback, while 'closed' and 'readonly' errors become Promise rejections for await compatibility.
TursoAdapter lazily loads @libsql/client via dynamic import() on first use — consumers who only use SqliteAdapter never load the Turso driver.

The @libsql/client dependency was added as a root devDependency (not in store-adapter's own devDependencies) because pnpm's --filter doesn't yet recognize the new nx project. This can be moved to the package's devDependencies once nx recognizes the project.
sqlite-vec cannot be loaded with TursoAdapter — different native binding ABI. Consumer code must narrow to SqliteAdapter before calling unwrap().
The `pragmaGet` return type is `Promise<unknown>` on the interface — SqliteAdapter returns whatever better-sqlite3's pragma() returns, TursoAdapter extracts the first column of the first row.
